issue_context.summary: A layered Keyboard Manager configuration that remaps Caps Lock to Right Ctrl and then maps Right Ctrl chords eventually leaks original Q/E/W/A/S/D input instead of the remapped arrows and Ctrl+Arrow outputs.
known_information: The report provides exact remaps and a GIF.
Failure occurs while Caps Lock is held across multiple mapped action keys.
No current-version follow-up or linked pull request exists.
inferences: The engine may release or fail to recognize the synthetic Right Ctrl modifier state after one target shortcut, allowing subsequent physical action keys through.
issue_context.analysis: This is a deterministic chained-remap state-machine scenario that maintainers can reproduce locally. Current Keyboard Manager explicitly distinguishes physical, remapped, and injected state, so the first action should be a targeted event-sequence test rather than a generic log request.
initial_investigation: KeyboardEventHandlers.cpp tracks injected events and source/target modifier state across shortcut remaps.
Related issue 20368 discussed Ctrl+Left/Ctrl+Right and Quick Accent but did not establish that it is the same chained-remap failure.

proposed_fixes.title: Preserve synthetic modifier state across chained shortcut remaps
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The remapped Caps Lock-to-Right-Ctrl state may not remain represented as a held source modifier after a shortcut target completes, so later action keys bypass the matching shortcut and emit their originals.
plan: Add a low-level event test for the exact Caps Lock/Right Ctrl and W/A/S/D/Q/E mapping graph.
Separate physical source-key lifetime from each invoked target shortcut's cleanup and suppress original action keys while the synthetic modifier remains held.
Guarantee all injected modifiers are released exactly once when Caps Lock is released or remapping is reset.
verification: Hold Caps Lock and cycle through all six action keys repeatedly; verify only arrows and Ctrl+Arrow events are emitted and no modifier remains stuck.

confidence.rationale: The state-machine hypothesis matches the sequence, but the old report needs a current event trace to locate the precise cleanup branch.
